- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral/negative.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and price is falling, model often underestimates drop; add 0.5–1% buffer to forecast to account for mean reversion.  
- Model frequently overreacts to recent volatility; if 3–5 consecutive days show high sentiment swings, apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows strong positive sentiment followed by a sharp drop, model often fails to adjust; apply “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per day after sentiment drops below 0.5.
